rubrics.criterion: The flattened 2D drawing routines on the main canvas — the mesh drawing, the instanced mesh drawing and the bounded text drawing — are all decomposed: each entry point now reads as an orchestration over well-scoped helper methods, instead of one contiguous body that performs pipeline selection, bind-group/layout construction, uniform-arena allocation, image/text bind-group setup and render-pass driving itself.
rubrics.rationale: These are the entry points whose setup layers were copied wholesale into single bodies; a solution that leaves any of the three as a wall of inline machinery has not restored the drawing layer's structure on the 2D canvas, which is the primary scope of this task.

rubrics.criterion: The 3D canvas mesh drawing and instanced mesh drawing paths receive the same restoration: their absorbed setup (3D pipeline construction, bind-group/layout cache population, image bind-group shaping, and the uniform-arena bump on the instanced variant) is extracted into helpers at the owning layer, and the 3D feature still gates this code.
rubrics.rationale: The 3D drawing paths absorbed the same helper chains in their own feature-gated module; a repair that only untangles the 2D canvas leaves half of the drawing family flattened, and the default-feature test suite cannot reveal that.

rubrics.criterion: The extracted helpers each own one responsibility of the graphics stack (pipeline selection over the pipeline cache, bind-group and layout shaping over the bind-group/sampler caches, uniform allocation over the buffer arena, glyph measurement and text queueing over the text renderer) — the decomposition follows responsibility boundaries rather than being an arbitrary mechanical split of the long bodies into chunks of similar size.
rubrics.rationale: The task asks for a layered structure restored at the right abstraction level; splitting a several-hundred-line body at arbitrary line boundaries into fragments that still mix several subsystems would reduce line counts without restoring any delegation structure or ownership.

rubrics.criterion: Construction logic that is genuinely the same across the draw variants (mesh vs instanced vs the 3D twins) is now served by common, parameterized helper code — the near-identical listings of pipeline/bind-group construction that were pasted into several draw entry points are not re-created as one private copy per call site.
rubrics.rationale: The duplicated construction listings between sibling draw paths are the cross-location coordination this case requires: if each variant gets its own private copy of the extracted logic, the change-amplification and drift problem the task describes is preserved under new names.

rubrics.criterion: Low-level device and cache operations (render-pipeline creation, bind-group-layout and bind-group creation, lazy cache population, buffer creation for the uniform arena, glyph queueing) live inside the GPU subsystem helper methods (or equivalent functions in those owning modules) rather than being scattered across the draw entry points' bodies.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed regions reach directly into the lowest device layer from the drawing API surface; moving those operations to the layers that naturally own them (the cache, arena and text-renderer modules) is an associated adjustment the drawing-path fix cannot leave behind.

rubrics.criterion: Field visibility that was relaxed to crate-internal purely so the flattened draw methods could reach cache internals directly is tightened back toward private wherever the re-established helpers make that possible, without breaking compilation.
rubrics.rationale: The flat state forced open fields on the pipeline cache, bind-group cache, sampler cache, uniform arena and text payload solely to serve inline access; restoring encapsulation is the natural cleanup of that leftover, as long as the helper layout really permits it.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves in place (or newly introduces) comments that label stages of formerly inlined machinery — such as stage labels claiming a distinct 'textures' or 'arena bump' region — at sites where that machinery actually now lives behind a helper call, so descriptions contradict the new structure.
rubrics.rationale: The inlined bodies carried comments asserting a decomposition the contiguous code did not have; a real repair updates those descriptions, and stale ones actively mislead the next reader of the drawing code.

rubrics.criterion: The text drawing path's queue/flush discipline is broken by the extraction — e.g. queued text is no longer flushed before canvas-state setters apply, or the text pipeline's selection point moved to where queued text renders with a stale pipeline or blend state — changing observable text rendering.
rubrics.rationale: The bounded-text path interleaves queue-time steps (measurement, section assembly, pipeline selection) with the flush sentinel guarding every setter; this is the one place where moving code across the flush boundary changes visible behavior even when all tests still pass.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor changes which GPU objects get created or used: e.g. a draw path retains an unconditional construction in addition to the re-introduced lazy helper, a helper's cache key or descriptor contents differs from what the inlined code used, or a previously shared object gets created per call — altering lazy-init caching semantics.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed regions are lazily-cached constructions with exact key/descriptor semantics; duplicating or drifting one construction detail changes device state and cache behavior that no headless test observes.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is partial: at least one drawing path that had absorbed its setup remains in the flattened state (for example only the 3D paths, or only the text path, are left as contiguous walls of construction code) while other paths were decomposed.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening touched five entry points in two canvas implementations; solving only the most visible instances leaves the same problem where the default test suite cannot see it, which is the characteristic incomplete repair for this task.

rubrics.criterion: The real capability differences between the draw variants are fused or lost in the extraction — e.g. 3D-specific depth-tested/back-face-culled pipeline attributes, or the existence of a text-only pipeline variant, get merged into a single configuration that would change what one of the variants renders.
rubrics.rationale: The 2D, instanced, text and 3D paths genuinely differ in pipeline attributes and stages; a repair that parameterizes them must carry those differences as parameters or separate methods, not average them away.

rubrics.criterion: A shared or cleanup change leaves the feature-gated 3D-only drawing code inconsistent or uncompilable — for instance a helper signature or field visibility change whose 3D callers or 3D field usages were not adjusted together — while the default-feature build and tests stay green.
rubrics.rationale: The 3D module sits behind the `3d` feature that the recorded test command never enables, so cross-file cleanups are exactly where a silent inconsistency can hide in this repository.
